messages:
support_lead: Escalation from AcmeCorp — their /v1/generate route is seeing a clear jump in 95th and 99th latency since the runtime swap at ~09:05 UTC. Customers hitting 30s timeouts and retries. They say it started right after the 'runtime-agent v2.7.0' rollout. Adding initial logs and a sample request id: req=acme-req-9832. :rotating_light:

maria: Thanks — linking observability. Can someone pull the 95/99 traces for that tenant in us-east for the 09:00-09:40 window?

deploy-bot: rollout roll-2026-03-16-09 applied runtime-agent:v2.7.0 to pool=runtime-us-east-2 at 2026-03-16T09:05:12Z (hosts affected: 10).

alex: grabbing traces now. Quick thought: v2.7.0 includes a change to the auth prefetch + KV cache refactor — might be an auth cold-path causing heavy tail.

jamie: dashboard: https://observability.redwood.internal/d/single-tenant/AcmeCorp?from=2026-03-16T09:00:00Z&to=2026-03-16T09:40:00Z — 95th jumps from ~160ms to ~2.8s, 99th into 12s. Error rate (5xx) up 0.8pp.

alex: can we repro locally? support_lead can you give me a sample curl with headers the customer uses?

support_lead: sample curl pasted below (redacted keys):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "X-Tenant: acmecorp" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' -v
```

support_lead: They see the long tail intermittently, not every request. Mostly larger prompts but even small ones spike.

alex: repro steps I ran: 100 reqs/sec to tenant header acmecorp with a small prompt. After ~30s I see a subset hitting auth refresh and peaking latency. Stack trace points to auth->kv->http call chain where kv.get sometimes blocks ~8-10s.

jamie: pulling host-level metrics for the 10 hosts in roll-2026-03-16-09. CPU is fine, but io_wait on two hosts spiked around 09:08. Network retransmits slight bump.

maria: hypothesis list: 1) KV client change in v2.7.0 that retries differently causing head-of-line blocking; 2) auth prefetch race causing sync fetch on hot path; 3) unlucky affinity exposing a slow backend instance. Which one looks most likely?

alex: my bet is (1) + (2). The code path added a synchronous fallback that used the shared KV connection pool; under load that pool exhausts and some requests block.

ingram: we can test quickly: 1) reroute small percentage (5-10%) of AcmeCorp traffic to runtime-agent:v2.6.4 (previous) via weight override, 2) run synthetic replay against both and compare 95/99. I can submit the routing override.

srebot: created synthetic job synth-replay-acme-327659 at 2026-03-16T10:05Z — replaying historical 1m sample at 50x. Results will post in ~10m.

maria: also, can eng-runtime run a short patch that changes KV client to async fallback? If that's quick it could be pushed to canary but we want minimal blast radius.

alex: I have a tiny patch that flips fallback to background fetch (non-blocking) — will build and smoke test locally in 10m. If green, we can push to a single host to validate.

support_lead: AcmeCorp is asking for a mitigation now — they want traffic stable. Is a routing override feasible ASAP?

ingram: I applied a weight override: AcmeCorp -> runtime-agent:v2.6.4 = 90%, v2.7.0 = 10% at 2026-03-16T10:12Z. Watching.

jamie: after override: 95th drops to ~200ms within ~3 minutes, 99th down to ~1.2s. Error rate back near baseline. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

support_lead: forwarding to customer that we've applied a partial rollback and are continuing investigation. They asked if we plan full rollback.

maria: we should avoid full rollback until patch verification; partial weight override gives breathing room. Alex, status on patch?

alex: built patch and ran local synthetic — no regressions, and tail latency reduced in local test. I'll push to one host in the affected pool (host runtime-us-east-2-07) with runtime-agent:v2.7.0+fix-327 and run smoke.

deploy-bot: deploying runtime-agent:v2.7.0+fix-327 to runtime-us-east-2-07 (1/10) at 2026-03-16T10:22Z.

srebot: smoke synthetic against patched host shows 95th ~180ms, 99th ~950ms for the same replay sample.

ingram: if patch looks good on single host, I can ramp weights so more traffic uses fixed variant and reduce pressure on older nodes.

maria: plan: 1) ramp fixed variant to 50% over 10m, 2) monitor tenant 95/99 and error rate, 3) if stable, roll forward fixed image to remaining hosts; otherwise, full rollback. Documenting steps here.

support_lead: customer updated: "service improved after partial change, please keep us posted." They asked for postmortem and priors.

ingram: ramp to 50% started at 2026-03-16T10:30Z. Monitoring graphs look stable.

alex: I'll prepare a small changelog note for the fix and open a follow-up issue to investigate KV pool sizing for long-lived tenants.

maria: great. Keep updates in this thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

ingram: final check at 2026-03-16T11:10Z — 95/99 for AcmeCorp back to baseline; rolling full rollout of fixed image now.

support_lead: closing customer loop, will request SLA credit review if they ask.

maria: postmortem ticket created: infra/EVT-1329 — runtime-auth-kv-tail-regression; add timeline and repro steps.

alex: note for the postmortem: repro steps used synth-replay job synth-replay-acme-327659; local repro command:

```
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s --script=short_prompt.lua https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'X-Tenant: acmecorp' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

maria: thanks — nice work.

ingram: :rocket:"
